description:
Implement hybrid encryption for data at rest in stoa-mail. Decision: shared/NNTP content encrypted at the infrastructure level (EBS/RDS encryption under a site KMS key); user-specific personal data encrypted at the application level under per-user Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) wrapped by the site KMS key.

## Why this issue exists
Regulated customers (HIPAA, SOC2, PCI-DSS, GDPR) require that personal data be encrypted at rest with key management that supports: per-user isolation (compromise of one user's key does not expose others), cryptographic erasure on user deletion (GDPR right-to-erasure), and auditable key access logs. A single site-wide encryption key satisfies disk encryption requirements but not user isolation or cryptographic erasure.

## The hybrid policy (decided)

### Site KMS key (infrastructure-level, no app code change)
  - IPLD article blocks (content-addressed, shared across users — cannot be per-user)
  - activitypub_followers, activitypub_received (group-level, semi-public)
  - jmap_change_log (item_ids are CIDs, not content)
  - state_version (version counters only)
  - Full-text search index
  Mechanism: EBS volume encryption + RDS storage encryption, both using the site AWS KMS key.
  No application code changes required for these.

### Per-user DEK (application-level, this epic)
  - messages.raw_message, .envelope_from, .envelope_to (email body + addresses = PII)
  - user_flags (read/flagged state per user)
  - subscriptions (newsgroup list per user — reveals reading habits)
  - bearer_tokens.label (token labels may contain user-chosen strings)
  Mechanism: envelope encryption. One AES-256-GCM DEK per user, stored wrapped under
  the site KMS key in a new user_encryption_keys table.

## Envelope encryption pattern
  1. At user creation: generate random 32-byte DEK, call KMS Encrypt, store wrapped DEK
  2. At data read/write: call KMS Decrypt to unwrap DEK, use in-process, discard after request
  3. At user deletion: delete the user_encryption_keys row — all encrypted data becomes
     permanently unreadable (cryptographic erasure, satisfies GDPR Art. 17)

## KMS call budget
  One KMS Decrypt call per request that touches user data (not per row).
  Cache the unwrapped DEK for the request lifetime only — never persist plaintext DEK.
  AWS KMS pricing: ~$0.03/10,000 calls. At 1,000 req/day = ~$1/year. Not a concern.

## Out of scope
  - KMS key creation, IAM policy, key rotation schedule (infra)
  - EBS/RDS encryption enablement (infra)
  - Encrypting the full-text search index content (deferred — Tantivy index is derivative
    of messages, becomes stale after DEK deletion; document this gap)
  - Transit encryption (TLS — already present)

## Acceptance criteria
  - messages.raw_message, envelope_from, envelope_to are stored as authenticated
    ciphertext (AES-256-GCM); plaintext never written to DB
  - user_flags and subscriptions rows are encrypted under per-user DEK
  - Deleting a user's DEK row makes all their encrypted data unreadable (test: attempt
    decrypt after DEK deletion → error, not plaintext)
  - A local (in-process) key backend works in dev/test without AWS credentials
  - cargo test -p stoa-mail passes with local backend
title: Data at rest: hybrid encryption — site KMS key + per-user DEK
